rules.sentence: MAPCAs are often present in various CHDs that compromise pulmonary circulation, either due to severe pulmonary valvular or arterial stenosis or complete pulmonary atresia.

rules.disease: tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with pulmonary atresia (TOF/PA)
rules.sentence: Lesions frequently showing MAPCAs in their pathology are called "pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect." However, it is more descriptive to consider them as tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with pulmonary atresia (TOF/PA).

rules.disease: pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect (PA/VSD)
rules.sentence: Patients with varying phenotypic arrangements can also be correctly described as having pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect (PA/VSD).

rules.disease: tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with pulmonary atresia (TOF/PA)
rules.sentence: TOF/PA is a congenital heart defect that can also be referred to as "pseudo-truncus arteriosus."

rules.disease: tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with pulmonary atresia (TOF/PA)
rules.sentence: Thus, blood from both ventricles goes into the aorta.

rules.disease: tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with pulmonary atresia (TOF/PA)
rules.sentence: The pulmonary circulation is supplied through multiple MAPCAs or a PDA.

rules.disease: tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with pulmonary atresia (TOF/PA)
rules.sentence: Neonates can develop hypoxic symptoms if the PDA closes or if the MAPCAs are narrow or stenosed in severe cases.
